summary: WorldEntity duplicate diagnostics do not currently describe enough of both GenerationOrigin records to reproduce or distinguish a true StableId collision when kind and recipeKey happen to match. The architecture contract says duplicate registration emits a diagnostic describing both origins, but DuplicateIdentityDiagnostic retains only entityId, kinds, and recipe keys; worldId, optional regionId, generator, and generatorVersion are omitted. A collision across different worlds/generator versions with the same kind/recipeKey therefore produces indistinguishable diagnostic payloads. Consider carrying immutable existing/incoming origin snapshots (or equivalent complete repro fields) while preserving the bounded diagnostic history.
evidence: Docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: registry rejects duplicate live IDs, keeps first authoritative, and emits a diagnostic describing both origins.
Docs/ADR/0002-deterministic-reality.md: StableId collisions must be detectable by registries that know the canonical identity behind an ID.

main@914d0a2 DuplicateIdentityDiagnostic contains entityId, existing/incoming kind, and existing/incoming recipeKey only; register() has both full origin records available but does not retain worldId/regionId/generator/generatorVersion in the diagnostic.
The diagnostic history is already bounded/frozen, so expanding the retained plain-data repro identity need not change registry ownership semantics.
